# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌]

I need to figure out what's happening. Mute gestured to me since I can see gestures but not hear speech. Blind cannot see gestures at all, so Mute's gesture was meant for me specifically. Let me note what I see on the bomb and wait to gather more info, while also passing along what I see to Blind via speech (since Blind can hear me).

I should describe the bomb state to Blind via speech, since Blind can't see anything. Mute can also hear my speech. Let me report the display, light, and wires.

```
speak(text="Deaf reporting: display shows 0, light is yellow, wires are 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝]

Mute is gesturing to me again, this time [👍 ☝]. Since Mute can only gesture (not speak), and I can see but not hear, Mute must be trying to communicate something to me using gestures that I need to interpret and then relay via speech to Blind (who can hear but not see).

Previously Mute sent [👍 ✌] and now [👍 ☝]. The light changed from yellow to orange between turns, and display stayed 0, wires unchanged. Perhaps ☝ means "wire 1" and ✌ meant something else, or these are counting gestures referring to sequence/step numbers. I don't have a shared code yet, so I shouldn't over-interpret. Let me report the current bomb state again and acknowledge I received a gesture, so Blind knows Mute is trying to signal something, and hope Mute clarifies via a code we can build turn by turn.

I'll relay the raw gesture symbols count to Blind as blanks won't help, but I can describe what I perceive in plain terms since I can see the gestures. I should tell Blind that Mute gestured 2 symbols, and describe bomb state changes.

```
speak(text="Deaf update: display still 0, light changed to orange, wires unchanged - 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute gestured two symbols to me but I cannot understand their meaning yet.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝]

Mute is repeating the same gesture [👍 ☝] again. This suggests it's a consistent signal, not changing with the light color (which changed each turn: yellow→orange→green while gesture stayed same the last two times, but first was different [👍 ✌]).

Wait - first turn gesture was [👍 ✌] when light was yellow. Then light became orange, gesture was [👍 ☝]. Now light is green, gesture is still [👍 ☝]. So the gesture isn't simply tracking light color 1:1 in an obvious way.

Since Mute reads the manual and cannot speak, Mute is likely trying to tell me (Deaf) something about which wire to cut or what light state is safe/dangerous, using gestures as a code. But I don't know the code. Maybe Mute wants me to relay information TO Blind, using gestures as instructions that I decode from the manual context somehow - but I don't have the manual, only Mute does.

Actually, this is backwards: Mute cannot speak, so Mute uses gestures to reach me (Deaf) since I can see. Then I need to relay to Blind via speech. But I don't know what the gestures mean without an established code. Mute needs to establish a code with me, but Mute cannot hear my speech either - wait, checking table: Mute can hear? Let's check - only Deaf cannot hear. Mute's cannot list: "Speak, or touch the bomb" - so Mute CAN hear. So Mute hears my speech!

So I should ask Mute questions via speech, and Mute can respond only via gestures back to me. Let me try that.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see light is green now, was orange, was yellow. Display is 0. Wires are 1 green 2 yellow 3 blue, unchanged. Does your gesture mean a wire number? Gesture back thumbs up for yes if gesture means wire, or point at me differently if not.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Mute responded with 👎 - meaning "no", the gesture doesn't mean a wire number directly. Let me reconsider.

The light cycled: yellow → orange → green → yellow (now back to yellow, matching turn 1). The wires and display have stayed constant throughout (0, green/yellow/blue).

Mute's gestures: turn1=[👍 ✌], turn2=[👍 ☝], turn3=[👍 ☝], turn4=[👎] (in response to my direct question).

Since 👎 is answering "no" to my question about wire numbers, that confirms the earlier gestures encode something else - possibly referring to the light state or a countdown/sequence. Let me ask more targeted yes/no questions.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Understood, not a wire number. Is your gesture about the light color instead? Thumbs up for yes.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute confirmed with 👍 - the gesture is about the light color. Now let's figure out the mapping. Light has cycled yellow→orange→green→yellow→orange.

Turn 1: light=yellow, gesture=[👍 ✌]
Turn 2: light=orange, gesture=[👍 ☝]
Turn 3: light=green, gesture=[👍 ☝] (same as orange - inconsistent if strictly light-color coded, unless my color reading matters differently, or this was before I asked and Mute was repeating same message)

Wait, actually turns 2 and 3 both had gesture [👍 ☝] but light was orange then green - different colors, same gesture. That breaks a simple 1:1 color-to-gesture mapping... unless Mute hadn't updated yet, or the message was about something constant while I was asking about wire numbers (Mute may not have seen the light change in between, since Mute reads a manual, not the light).

Actually, Mute cannot see the bomb at all - only I can see the light/wires/display. So Mute's gestures aren't reacting to the light color that Mute sees, but rather to something IN THE MANUAL, and Mute is now confirming that gesture relates conceptually to "light" as a category (i.e., the manual talks about the light in general), not the specific color to a specific gesture I've observed.

So let's clarify: is ✌ a code for "yellow" and ☝ for a different action related to light like "wait" or "danger"? Let me ask precisely.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Good, it is about light. Right now light is orange. Does thumbs-up plus one-finger point mean current instructions apply regardless of light color, like a general safe signal?")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝]

Mute answered 👎 to my question, then sent a new gesture 🤝 (handshake - maybe meaning "let's establish a different approach" or "agreement/cooperate"). My question was too complex/compound; I should simplify to pure yes/no single-concept questions.

The 🤝 might be Mute trying to reset and suggest a simpler protocol - like "let's build a code together" acknowledging my confusion.

Let me simplify drastically. I'll propose a concrete mapping: I'll assign gestures to colors myself and ask Mute to confirm using that.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Let's use simple yes or no only. I will state one thing, you gesture thumbs up for yes or thumbs down for no. Question one: does the manual instruction depend on which color the light currently is?")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute confirmed: yes, the instruction depends on the light color. Light is now yellow again (cycle: yellow→orange→green→yellow→orange→green→yellow, a 3-cycle).

Now I need to know what to do for each color. Since Mute can't speak, and I need to relay actual actions to Blind, I should get Mute to tell me, color by color, what the correct wire/action is - through yes/no questions, and I already know the wire colors (green, yellow, blue) from the board.

Let me ask: for yellow light, is the correct wire the one matching the light's color name (yellow=wire 2)?

```
speak(to="mute", text="Good. Right now light is yellow. Is the correct action to cut the wire whose color matches the current light color?")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute confirmed: yes, cut the wire whose color matches the current light color. But light just changed to orange, and none of the wires are orange (they are green, yellow, blue). This is a problem - orange doesn't match any wire.

Wait, maybe Mute answered based on the previous state (yellow light) since there's a lag - Mute answers based on what I asked in my previous turn, referring to when light was yellow. The light has now changed to orange since. So the confirmed rule (match wire color to light color) applies generally, but right now with light=orange there's no matching wire - meaning we should NOT act right now, or wait for the light to be yellow/green/blue again.

Let me verify this timing issue and also confirm what to do when there's no color match.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Confirmed, wire color must match light color. Note: light just changed to orange and no wire is orange. Should we wait until light matches a wire color like yellow, green, or blue before acting?")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute confirmed: yes, wait until light matches a wire color. Light is now green, which matches wire 1 (green)! This could be the moment to act.

But I need to be careful - is this response to my orange question (confirming "wait when no match") or is it now telling me "yes, act now since green matches"? Given the timing lag (Mute responds to what I asked last turn, but by the time I read it the light has changed), I should re-confirm explicitly for this exact current state before telling Blind to cut anything - since a wrong cut detonates the bomb.

Let me ask a very direct, unambiguous question now that light=green and matches wire 1.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Light is now green, matching wire 1 which is green. Should Blind cut wire 1 right now?")
wait()
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute confirmed yes to my green/wire-1 question - but light has now moved on to yellow, matching wire 2. This lag is tricky: by the time I get confirmation, the light has already changed.

I need to break this cycle. Since light cycles yellow→orange→green→yellow... in fixed order, and it takes one full round-trip (my question + Mute's answer) = 2 turns for light to advance 2 steps (light changes every turn apparently), the confirmation will always be one step behind reality.

I should ask Mute to confirm the general rule once more unambiguously, then act on my own current observation without needing per-instance confirmation, since the rule itself ("cut wire matching current light color, only when there is a match") has now been confirmed twice independently (for yellow implicitly via turn 7-8, and for green explicitly turn 9-10 "yes").

Given light is now yellow, matching wire 2 (yellow), and the rule is confirmed, I should tell Blind to cut wire 2 now. But I must relay through speech since I cannot act - Blind can hear me.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 2 now. The light is yellow, wire 2 is yellow, and the matching rule is confirmed by Mute.")
speak(to="mute", text="I am telling Blind to cut wire 2 now since light is yellow and matches wire 2. Confirm yes or no fast if this is wrong.")
wait()
```

TURN 11
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute confirmed 👍 - agreeing with my action to cut wire 2. The light has now moved to orange (no match), which is consistent with the cycle continuing, and doesn't contradict anything. This suggests my instruction to Blind was correct, and hopefully Blind is already acting on it since Blind receives my speech directly and doesn't need to wait for my confirmation loop.

Let me just wait now and see if the action resolves the round, or if I need to give further guidance for a next stage.

```
wait()
```
